name: TX-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+24 partisan lean anchors the race firmly in Republican territory
Moran holds a roughly 70-to-1 fundraising advantage over Prince ($2.4M vs $33K)
Prediction markets price the Republican at about 97%, with no outside spending on either side
No public polling exists, but nothing contradicts the fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's R+24 lean, Moran's overwhelming financial advantage, and market pricing near 97% Republican all point the same direction, and even a national environment tilted toward Democrats this cycle falls far short of closing a gap this wide.
model.watch: A major scandal involving Moran or a dramatic late shift in the national climate could narrow the race, though the district's fundamentals would likely still hold.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's first district is deeply Republican territory, and incumbent Nathaniel Moran enters the general election with every structural advantage. The district's partisan lean favors Republicans by roughly twenty-four points, and Moran has raised about $2.4 million while holding nearly $1 million on hand. Democrat Yolanda Prince has raised about $33,000, leaving her little capacity to compete on the airwaves, and no outside groups have invested in the race on either side.

No public polls cover the contest, but prediction markets price Moran's chances near ninety-seven percent. The national political environment leans toward Democrats this cycle, yet a shift of that size cannot come close to erasing a gap this large in a district this red. Barring an unexpected scandal or a dramatic change in the national climate, Moran is positioned to win comfortably.
